name: frontend-design
description: Build or revise product-specific web interfaces with design-system discipline and rendered verification. Use for HTML, CSS, JavaScript, or TypeScript frontend work including marketing pages, dashboards, forms, settings, authentication, components, empty states, and responsive UI.
---

# Frontend Design

Treat frontend design as a closed system: understand the product and its visual language before adding UI. Distinctiveness should come from product evidence, information hierarchy, and precise composition instead of generic decoration.

## Authority

Explicit user requirements and approved design specifications govern first. Existing project components and conventions govern next. Use this package's defaults only to fill gaps. Ask one focused question when those authorities conflict; never create a second visual language silently.

## 1. Detect the design context

Inspect relevant source before planning markup. Find theme and token files, typography and icon conventions, layout primitives, component libraries, nearby pages, and frontend validation scripts.

| Mode | Evidence | Response |
|---|---|---|
| Existing system | Several token and component categories are established | Reuse them |
| Partial system | Some visual conventions exist | Preserve them and fill only uncovered needs |
| Greenfield | No meaningful visual system exists | Define the smallest semantic token set and reusable primitives needed for this task |
| Ambiguous | Signals conflict | Ask which direction governs the work |

Continue only after recording the mode and the files that support it.

## 2. Select an archetype

Read [`../../standards/page-archetypes.md`](../../standards/page-archetypes.md) completely. Choose the closest archetype before implementation. A feature inside an established application normally uses the component or application-feature archetype unless it replaces an entire page.

The selection is complete when every required region or state is accounted for and genuinely inapplicable items are marked as such.

## 3. Define hierarchy and evidence

Use [`../../standards/task-brief.md`](../../standards/task-brief.md) to state the working contract:

```text
page purpose and user
primary task and primary action
optional secondary action
required content and section order
concrete product evidence
components and tokens to reuse
responsive behavior
accessibility requirements
```

Prefer a real product interface, then real data, code or terminal output, a technical or process diagram, and finally a product-specific illustration. When interface copy changes, read [`../../standards/content-standards.md`](../../standards/content-standards.md) completely before drafting it.

Move on when every section supports the primary task and the archetype's first viewport contains the required product evidence.

## 4. Establish implementation constraints

Read these files completely before changing frontend source:

- [`../../standards/frontend-standards.md`](../../standards/frontend-standards.md)
- [`../../standards/forbidden-patterns.md`](../../standards/forbidden-patterns.md)

An existing system owns component behavior and visual values. Use approved components with named variants. Treat shared design-system source and standards as protected during product UI work. If a required capability is missing, report the exact gap and ask before changing the design system or adding a one-off variant. In partial and greenfield systems, place new values in reusable semantic tokens rather than scattering raw values through feature code.

Implementation may begin once every component and visual value has an established source or one clearly defined new semantic source.

## 5. Build the smallest complete slice

Implement in reading order. Preserve semantic HTML and keyboard behavior. Keep focus visible and honor reduced-motion preferences. Cover each state the feature can enter, including disabled or selected behavior and any loading, empty, success, or error result. Keep action priority and content order intact as the viewport changes.

Motion should explain feedback or continuity. A card should mark a useful boundary or grouped interaction.

Finish this step only when the requested flow works through every applicable state and representative width.

## 6. Run repository checks

Run the actual frontend checks found in step 1. Exercise available linting and compilation, behavior tests, accessibility checks, and visual tests. Do not invent script names. Do not update visual baselines unless the task explicitly authorizes a reviewed baseline change.

Every available check must pass. For an unavailable category, record the evidence showing that the repository does not provide it.

## 7. Verify rendered output

Capture the affected interface with project browser tooling when possible. Otherwise use another available browser automation tool. Review these representative viewports:

```text
390 x 844
768 x 1024
1440 x 900
```

Inspect primary interactions and visible focus where practical. Read [`../../standards/visual-review-rubric.md`](../../standards/visual-review-rubric.md) completely, score the render, fix each critical failure and applicable violation, then capture the corrected result once.

When browser access is unavailable, apply the same rubric to source and state that rendered verification could not run. Completion requires a passing review or a concrete external blocker for every remaining failure.

## Completion report

State the archetype and context mode. Name reused or added system resources, the product evidence shown, every command and result, screenshot paths or the browser limitation, and any unresolved design-system capability or external blocker.

# Software Design

Apply these principles when architecture or abstraction quality is a material part of the task.

## Two Modes

### Writing New Code

Apply these principles in order of impact.

#### Think strategically

Invest in design instead of stopping when the code first works. Produce a clean design that works, and spend 10–20% of the effort on design improvements.

#### Create deep modules

Each module should provide powerful functionality behind a simple interface. A few deep methods beat many shallow ones. Ask whether the interface is simpler than the implementation.

#### Hide information

Each module should encapsulate design decisions that remain invisible through its interface. If one decision appears in several modules, reorganize the code until that decision has one home.

#### Make interfaces general-purpose

Design an interface broad enough to support current uses while keeping its functionality focused. Ask for the simplest interface that covers every current need.

#### Give each layer a different abstraction

Adjacent layers should operate at different abstraction levels. Remove pass-through methods that delegate with the same signature.

#### Pull complexity downwards

Handle complexity inside the module instead of pushing it to callers. A simple interface matters more than a simple implementation.

#### Define errors out of existence

Redefine APIs so avoidable error conditions cannot arise. Mask low-level exceptions and consolidate their handling. Reserve crashes for unrecoverable failures.

#### Design it twice

Consider at least two radically different approaches before committing. Compare their strengths and costs. Apply this comparison to interfaces and implementations, then consider the broader system decomposition.

#### Name precisely

Names should create a clear mental image of an entity's purpose. Avoid vague choices such as `data`, `result`, `info`, or `tmp`. Name booleans with predicates such as `isConnected` instead of a state label such as `status`.

#### Be consistent

Use the same name for the same purpose everywhere. Reuse established coding patterns and conventions. Consistency reduces the reader's cognitive work.

#### Make code obvious

Code is obvious when a reader's first guess about its behaviour is correct. Choose precise names and follow established patterns. Use whitespace to expose structure, and comment only where the code cannot explain itself.

#### Write comments first

Write interface comments before implementation. A method that needs a long descriptive comment has a complex interface and should be redesigned. Comments should preserve information that code cannot represent.

### Reviewing Existing Code

Scan for these red flags in the listed order.

#### Shallow modules

Look for interfaces as complex as their implementations, many trivial methods, or classes with little functionality.

#### Information leakage

Find design decisions repeated across modules. A change to one detail should not require coordinated edits across several classes.

#### Temporal decomposition

Check for code organized around operation order instead of information hiding, such as separate read and write classes for one format.

#### Pass-through methods

Flag methods that only call another method with the same signature, especially when delegation accounts for half or more of a class's methods.

#### Overexposure

A common operation should not force callers to understand rare features. Default information that callers should not have to provide.

#### Conjoined methods

Flag a method when understanding it requires reading another method's implementation.

#### Repetition

Find non-trivial code patterns duplicated in several places.

#### Vague or hard-to-pick names

Flag names broad enough to describe many entities. Difficulty finding a precise name often means the entity has too many responsibilities.

#### Comment problems

Find comments that restate the code or expose implementation details in interface documentation. Long, complicated descriptions may reveal a poor abstraction.

#### Special-general mixture

Keep specialized use-case code out of a general-purpose mechanism.

#### Nonobvious code

Flag behaviour that a quick reading cannot reveal, including surprising side effects.

#### Too many exceptions

Look for exceptions the caller cannot handle and error paths longer than the normal path. Redefine operations when doing so can eliminate error conditions.

For the full checklist, read `references/red-flags.md`.

## References

`references/principles.md` covers all 15 design principles. It includes examples and techniques, along with the reasoning behind each principle. Read it when applying a specific principle or when deeper context is needed.

`references/red-flags.md` organizes every red flag by category. Read it during code review to check systematically for design problems.

## 14. Spawn workflow

Implement spawn as an idempotent, recoverable operation.

### Step 1: Authorize and validate

Derive the parent from the active authenticated execution context.

Validate:

- Parent exists
- Parent belongs to the current tenant
- Parent runtime is available
- Feature flag is enabled
- Requested model exists at that runtime
- Task and context meet bounds
- Parent depth permits another level
- Direct-child, active-descendant, tree-total, and per-turn limits permit another child
- Parent repository and workspace are valid

Use `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` around limit checks and delegation reservation so concurrent spawn calls cannot exceed limits.

### Step 2: Reserve the delegation

Insert:

```text
status = provisioning
child_session_id = null
child_workspace_id = null
```

Idempotency:

```text
UNIQUE(parent_session_id, idempotency_key)
```

On retry:

- Return the existing queued, running, or terminal child.
- Resume or reconcile a provisioning record.
- Return a stable failed result for a failed reservation.
- Require a new idempotency key for a deliberate new attempt.

### Step 3: Capture the parent base

For a clean parent, resolve `HEAD`.

For a dirty parent, create a hidden snapshot without touching the real index, branch, or working tree.

Suggested algorithm:

1. Create a private temporary index file.
2. Set `GIT_INDEX_FILE` only for the snapshot subprocesses.
3. Run `git read-tree HEAD` against the alternate index.
4. Apply existing secret guardrails.
5. Run `git add -A -- .` against the alternate index.
6. Run `git write-tree`.
7. Run `git commit-tree` with the parent `HEAD` as parent.
8. Update `refs/yinshi/snapshots/<delegation-id>`.
9. Delete the temporary index.
10. Verify the parent `HEAD`, branch, real index, and working tree are unchanged.

Initial restrictions:

- Reject dirty submodules.
- Reject snapshots over configured file-count or byte limits.
- Exclude ignored files.
- Reject protected secret paths.
- Preserve tracked symlinks as Git symlinks.
- Support empty repositories through the existing empty-root logic.
- Record `base_kind` as `head` or `snapshot`.

### Step 4: Create the child worktree

Generate:

```text
yinshi/thread-<short-delegation-id>
```

Create the child branch and worktree from the exact base commit.

Insert a workspace row:

```text
kind = delegated
parent_workspace_id = parent.workspace_id
```

### Step 5: Create the child session

In one transaction:

1. Insert the child session against the child workspace.
2. Set title and model.
3. Update the delegation with child session and workspace IDs.
4. Set delegation state to `queued`.
5. Commit.

### Step 6: Start the initial child run

Build a bounded child prompt:

```text
You are a delegated Yinshi child thread.

Role:
<role>

Task:
<task>

Relevant context:
<context>

Execution rules:
- Work only inside your assigned workspace.
- Do not merge into or modify the parent workspace.
- Complete the requested task and run relevant tests.
- Before finishing, call report_thread_result with a concise summary,
  tests performed, and remaining warnings.
```

Start the prompt through the existing durable prompt journal.

Derive the initial prompt-run idempotency key from the delegation ID.

After successful scheduling:

```text
delegation.status = running
delegation.started_at = current timestamp
```

When startup fails, mark the delegation `failed` and retain the child workspace for inspection.

### Step 7: Finalize the child result

When the child reaches a terminal prompt-run state:

1. Load the delegation.
2. Create a private alternate index based on the child's `base_commit`.
3. Add the child's final worktree state to the alternate index.
4. Write the final tree.
5. Create one synthetic result commit whose parent is `base_commit`.
6. Update `refs/yinshi/results/<delegation-id>`.
7. Compute changed files from `base_commit` to `result_commit`.
8. Seal the reported or derived result.
9. Move the delegation to its terminal state.
10. Notify active waiters.

The synthetic result commit represents the complete final delta even when the child created several commits or left changes uncommitted.

"""Read-only thread projections over existing sessions and delegations.

A thread is a projection over an existing ``sessions`` row. Parentage comes
exclusively from ``thread_delegations.child_session_id``. Each metadata read
resolves one bounded root-tree snapshot (``_RootTreeSnapshot``) that owns root

ACTIVE_DELEGATION_STATUSES: Final[frozenset[str]] = frozenset(
    {"provisioning", "queued", "running", "cancelling"}
)
TERMINAL_DELEGATION_STATUSES: Final[frozenset[str]] = frozenset(
    {"completed", "failed", "cancelled", "interrupted"}

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)

    max_depth: int
    max_direct_children: int
    max_active_descendants: int
    max_total_threads: int

    @classmethod
    def from_settings(cls) -> _TreeLimits:
        """Capture the currently configured thread limits."""
        settings = get_settings()
        return cls(
            max_depth=settings.thread_max_depth,
            max_direct_children=settings.thread_max_direct_children,
            max_active_descendants=settings.thread_max_active_descendants,
            max_total_threads=settings.thread_max_total,
        )

    def allows_spawn(
        self,
        depth: int,
        own_children: int,
        active_descendants: int,
        total_threads: int,
    ) -> bool:
        """Return whether one candidate spawn stays inside every limit."""
        return (
            depth < self.max_depth
            and own_children < self.max_direct_children
            and active_descendants < self.max_active_descendants
            and total_threads < self.max_total_threads

    role: str
    status: str
    initiator: str

            role=str(row["role"]),

    member_chain: tuple[sqlite3.Row, ...]

        """Return the visible direct-child count for one session."""
        return int(self.child_counts.get(session_id, 0))

    def active_child_count(self, session_id: str) -> int:
        """Return the visible active direct-child count for one session."""
        return int(self.active_child_counts.get(session_id, 0))

            self.active_descendants,

def _ancestry_chain(
    db: sqlite3.Connection,
    session_id: str,
    owner_email: str | None = None,
) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
    """Return child-delegation rows from this session up to its visible root."""
    chain: list[sqlite3.Row] = []
    visited: set[str] = {session_id}
    current: str | None = session_id
    while current is not None:
        delegation = _child_delegation(db, current)
        if delegation is None:
            break
        parent_id = str(delegation["parent_session_id"])
        if owner_email is not None:
            parent = db.execute(
                "SELECT r.owner_email FROM sessions s "
                "JOIN workspaces w ON s.workspace_id = w.id "
                "JOIN repos r ON w.repo_id = r.id WHERE s.id = ?",
                (parent_id,),
            ).fetchone()
            if parent is None or parent["owner_email"] not in {None, owner_email}:
                raise ThreadNotFoundError(session_id)
        if parent_id in visited:
            raise ThreadCycleError("thread parentage records contain a cycle")
        chain.append(delegation)
        visited.add(parent_id)
        current = parent_id
        if len(chain) > _ANCESTRY_HOP_LIMIT:
            raise ThreadCycleError("thread parentage ancestry exceeds the hop limit")

    db: sqlite3.Connection,
    root_id: str,
    *,
    owner_email: str | None = None,
) -> list[_TreeDescendant]:
    """Collect visible descendant nodes with strict depth and node bounds."""
    nodes: list[_TreeDescendant] = []
    frontier: deque[tuple[str, int]] = deque([(root_id, 0)])
    seen: set[str] = {root_id}
    while frontier:
        parent_id, depth = frontier.popleft()
        if depth >= _ANCESTRY_HOP_LIMIT:
            continue
        for row in _direct_children(db, parent_id, owner_email=owner_email):
            child_id = str(row["id"])
            if child_id in seen:
                raise ThreadCycleError("thread parentage records contain a cycle")
            seen.add(child_id)
            nodes.append(_TreeDescendant(row=row, depth=depth + 1))
            if len(nodes) > _TREE_NODE_LIMIT:
                raise ThreadTreeSizeError("thread tree exceeds the size bound")
            frontier.append((child_id, depth + 1))
    return nodes

def _normalize_session_row(db: Any, row: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Normalize stored session models and persist repairs on read."""
    normalized_row = dict(row)
    original_model = normalized_row["model"]
    normalized_model = normalize_model_ref(original_model)
    if normalized_model != original_model:
        db.execute(
            "UPDATE sessions SET model = ? WHERE id = ?", (normalized_model, normalized_row["id"])
        )
        db.commit()
        normalized_row["model"] = normalized_model
    if "pi_context_version" not in normalized_row or normalized_row["pi_context_version"] is None:
        normalized_row["pi_context_version"] = 0
    return normalized_row


def _list_workspace_files(workspace_path: str) -> list[str]:
    """List workspace files while excluding bulky build directories."""
    if not os.path.isdir(workspace_path):
        return []

    files: list[str] = []
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(workspace_path):
        dirnames[:] = sorted(dirname for dirname in dirnames if dirname not in _EXCLUDED_DIRS)
        for filename in sorted(filenames):
            relative_path = os.path.relpath(
                os.path.join(dirpath, filename),
                workspace_path,
            )
            files.append(relative_path)
            if len(files) >= _TREE_FILE_LIMIT:
                files.sort()
                return files

    files.sort()
    return files

class RequestBodyLimitMiddleware:
    """Reject declared or streamed HTTP bodies above a process-wide limit."""

    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp, *, body_bytes_max: int) -> None:
        if body_bytes_max <= 0:
            raise ValueError("body_bytes_max must be positive")
        self._app = app
        self._body_bytes_max = body_bytes_max

    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
        if scope["type"] != "http":
            await self._app(scope, receive, send)
            return

        headers = {key.lower(): value for key, value in scope.get("headers", [])}
        content_length = headers.get(b"content-length")
        if content_length is not None:
            try:
                declared_bytes = int(content_length)
            except ValueError:
                await Response(status_code=400)(scope, receive, send)
                return
            if declared_bytes > self._body_bytes_max:
                await Response(status_code=413)(scope, receive, send)
                return

        received_bytes = 0

        async def limited_receive() -> Message:
            nonlocal received_bytes
            message = await receive()
            if message["type"] == "http.request":
                received_bytes += len(message.get("body", b""))
                if received_bytes > self._body_bytes_max:
                    raise _RequestBodyTooLarge
            return message

        try:
            await self._app(scope, limited_receive, send)
        except _RequestBodyTooLarge:
            await Response(status_code=413)(scope, receive, send)


class _RequestBodyTooLarge(Exception):

        DELEGATION_STATUS_INTERRUPTED,
    }

        *,
        parent_session_id: str,
        body: ThreadChildCreate,
    ) -> ThreadSpawnOutcome:
        """Reserve, provision, and attach one manual child thread."""
        if not isinstance(parent_session_id, str) or not parent_session_id.strip():
            raise ValueError("parent_session_id must be a non-empty string")
        reservation = await run_db_operation_for_request(
            request,
            lambda db: self._reserve(db, parent_session_id, body),
        )
        if str(reservation["status"]) != DELEGATION_STATUS_PROVISIONING:
            return ThreadSpawnOutcome(
                delegation_id=str(reservation["id"]),
                status=str(reservation["status"]),
                child_session_id=(
                    None
                    if reservation["child_session_id"] is None
                    else str(reservation["child_session_id"])
                ),
            )
        outcome = await self._provision_and_attach(request, reservation=reservation)
        return outcome

    def _reserve(
        self,
        db: sqlite3.Connection,
        parent_session_id: str,
        body: ThreadChildCreate,
    ) -> sqlite3.Row:
        """Insert one provisioning delegation inside one immediate transaction."""
        db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        try:
            parent = db.execute(
                "SELECT id, workspace_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?",
                (parent_session_id,),
            ).fetchone()
            if parent is None:
                raise ThreadNotFoundError(parent_session_id)
            existing = db.execute(
                """SELECT * FROM thread_delegations
                   WHERE parent_session_id = ? AND idempotency_key = ?""",
                (parent_session_id, body.idempotency_key),
            ).fetchone()
            if existing is not None:
                db.rollback()
                _assert_request_matches(existing, body)
                return existing
            db.execute(
                """INSERT INTO thread_delegations (
                       parent_session_id, idempotency_key, initiator,
                       title, task, context, role,
                       requested_model, requested_thinking, status
                   ) VALUES (?, ?, 'user', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                (
                    parent_session_id,
                    body.idempotency_key,
                    body.title.strip(),
                    body.task.strip(),
                    None if body.context is None else body.context.strip(),
                    body.role,
                    normalize_model_ref(body.model),
                    body.thinking,
                    DELEGATION_STATUS_PROVISIONING,
                ),
            )
            row = db.execute(
                """SELECT * FROM thread_delegations
                   WHERE parent_session_id = ? AND idempotency_key = ?""",
                (parent_session_id, body.idempotency_key),
            ).fetchone()
            db.commit()
            return row
        except BaseException:
            db.rollback()
            raise

    async def _provision_and_attach(
        self,
        request: Request,
        *,
        reservation: sqlite3.Row,
    ) -> ThreadSpawnOutcome:
        """Provision the child workspace, then attach the child session."""
        tenant = get_tenant(request)
        # Git must run with no open SQLite transaction.
        with get_db_for_request(request) as db:
            provisioned = await self._workspaces.provision_child(
                db,
                tenant,
                parent_workspace_id=str(reservation["parent_session_id"] and _parent_workspace_id(db, reservation)),
                delegation_id=str(reservation["id"]),
            )

        def attach(db: sqlite3.Connection) -> str:
            db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            try:
                cursor = db.execute(
                    """INSERT INTO sessions (workspace_id, status, model,
                                             pi_context_version, title)
                       VALUES (?, 'idle', ?, 1, ?)""",
                    (provisioned.workspace_id, reservation["requested_model"], reservation["title"]),
                )
                child_session_id = str(db.execute(
                    "SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE rowid = ?",
                    (cursor.lastrowid,),
                ).fetchone()["id"])
                db.execute(
                    """UPDATE thread_delegations
                       SET child_session_id = ?, child_workspace_id = ?,
                           base_kind = ?, base_commit = ?, snapshot_ref = ?,
                           status = ?
                       WHERE id = ? AND status = ?""",
                    (
                        child_session_id,
                        provisioned.workspace_id,
                        provisioned.base_kind,
                        provisioned.base_commit,
                        provisioned.snapshot_ref,
                        DELEGATION_STATUS_QUEUED,
                        reservation["id"],
                        DELEGATION_STATUS_PROVISIONING,
                    ),
                )
                db.commit()
                return child_session_id
            except BaseException:
                db.rollback()
                raise

        child_session_id = await run_db_operation_for_request(request, attach)
        return ThreadSpawnOutcome(
            delegation_id=str(reservation["id"]),
            status=DELEGATION_STATUS_QUEUED,
            child_session_id=child_session_id,
        )


def _assert_request_matches(row: sqlite3.Row, body: ThreadChildCreate) -> None:
    """Reject one idempotency key reuse whose normalized request differs."""
    stored = {
        "title": str(row["title"] or "").strip(),
        "task": str(row["task"] or "").strip(),
        "context": (None if row["context"] is None else str(row["context"]).strip() or None),
        "role": str(row["role"]),
        "model": normalize_model_ref(str(row["requested_model"] or "")),
        "thinking": (
            None if row["requested_thinking"] is None else str(row["requested_thinking"])
        ),
    }
    incoming = {
        "title": body.title.strip(),
        "task": body.task.strip(),
        "context": None if body.context is None else body.context.strip() or None,
        "role": body.role,
        "model": normalize_model_ref(body.model),
        "thinking": body.thinking,
    }
    if stored != incoming:
        raise ThreadIdempotencyConflictError(
            "idempotency key was already used with a different request",
        )


def _parent_workspace_id(db: sqlite3.Connection, reservation: sqlite3.Row) -> str:
    """Resolve the parent session's workspace id."""
    row = db.execute(
        "SELECT workspace_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?",
        (str(reservation["parent_session_id"]),),
    ).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        raise ThreadNotFoundError(str(reservation["parent_session_id"]))
    return str(row["workspace_id"])

"""Thread orchestration lifecycle policy and spawn workflow tests."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import uuid

import pytest
from fastapi import Request

from tests.test_thread_workspaces import head_commit, seed_parent_stack
from yinshi.models import ThreadChildCreate

from yinshi.services.thread_lifecycle import (
    cancellation_target,
    can_transition,
    initial_run_idempotency_key,
    is_terminal_delegation_status,
)


def test_terminal_delegation_status_set_is_exact() -> None:
    """Only completed, failed, cancelled, and interrupted are terminal."""
    assert is_terminal_delegation_status("completed")
    assert is_terminal_delegation_status("failed")
    assert is_terminal_delegation_status("cancelled")
    assert is_terminal_delegation_status("interrupted")
    assert not is_terminal_delegation_status("provisioning")
    assert not is_terminal_delegation_status("queued")
    assert not is_terminal_delegation_status("running")
    assert not is_terminal_delegation_status("cancelling")


def test_cancellation_losing_to_completion_preserves_completion() -> None:
    """A cancelling delegation may still resolve to completed."""
    assert can_transition("cancelling", "completed")


def test_cancellation_targets_are_stable_per_status() -> None:
    """Cancellation resolves each status to its plan-stable target."""
    assert cancellation_target("provisioning") == "cancelled"
    assert cancellation_target("queued") == "cancelled"
    assert cancellation_target("running") == "cancelling"
    assert cancellation_target("cancelling") == "cancelling"
    assert cancellation_target("completed") == "completed"
    assert cancellation_target("failed") == "failed"
    assert cancellation_target("cancelled") == "cancelled"
    assert cancellation_target("interrupted") == "interrupted"


def test_initial_run_idempotency_key_is_deterministic_canonical_uuid() -> None:
    """The initial child run derives one stable canonical UUID from the delegation."""
    delegation_id = "d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f801"
    first = initial_run_idempotency_key(delegation_id)
    assert first == initial_run_idempotency_key(delegation_id)
    assert str(uuid.UUID(first)) == first
    assert first != initial_run_idempotency_key("d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f802")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        initial_run_idempotency_key("not-a-delegation-id")


def _orchestration_request() -> Request:
    """Build one minimal request carrying no tenant, like prompt-journal tests."""
    from types import SimpleNamespace

    app = SimpleNamespace(state=SimpleNamespace())
    return Request(
        {
            "type": "http",
            "http_version": "1.1",
            "method": "POST",
            "scheme": "http",
            "path": "/",
            "raw_path": b"/",
            "query_string": b"",
            "headers": [],
            "client": ("127.0.0.1", 1),
            "server": ("127.0.0.1", 80),
            "app": app,
            "state": {},
        }
    )


def test_spawn_child_reserves_and_provisions_a_queued_child(db, git_repo) -> None:
    """One spawn reserves, provisions, and attaches a queued child thread."""
    from yinshi.services.thread_orchestration import ThreadOrchestrationService

    seed_parent_stack(db, git_repo)
    service = ThreadOrchestrationService()
    body = ThreadChildCreate(
        idempotency_key=str(uuid.uuid4()),
        title="Implement OAuth validation",
        task="Implement state validation.",
        role="implementation",
        model="model-x",
        start_immediately=False,
    )

    outcome = asyncio.run(
        service.spawn_child(
            _orchestration_request(),
            parent_session_id="parent-session",
            body=body,
        )
    )

    delegation = db.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM thread_delegations WHERE id = ?", (outcome.delegation_id,)
    ).fetchone()
    assert delegation is not None
    assert delegation["status"] == "queued"
    assert delegation["initiator"] == "user"
    assert delegation["base_kind"] == "head"
    assert delegation["base_commit"] == head_commit(git_repo)
    child = db.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM sessions WHERE id = ?", (delegation["child_session_id"],)
    ).fetchone()
    assert child is not None
    assert child["title"] == "Implement OAuth validation"
    assert child["model"] == "model-x"
    workspace = db.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM workspaces WHERE id = ?", (delegation["child_workspace_id"],)
    ).fetchone()
    assert workspace is not None
    assert workspace["kind"] == "delegated"
    assert workspace["parent_workspace_id"] == "parent-ws"
    assert workspace["branch"] == f"yinshi/thread-{outcome.delegation_id[:8]}"
    assert child["workspace_id"] == workspace["id"]
    assert (
        db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM prompt_runs").fetchone()["n"] == 0
    )


def test_duplicate_spawn_with_same_key_returns_the_same_child(db, git_repo) -> None:
    """One idempotency key resolves to exactly one delegation and child."""
    from yinshi.services.thread_orchestration import ThreadOrchestrationService

    seed_parent_stack(db, git_repo)
    service = ThreadOrchestrationService()
    body = ThreadChildCreate(
        idempotency_key=str(uuid.uuid4()),
        title="Implement OAuth validation",
        task="Implement state validation.",
        start_immediately=False,
    )

    first = asyncio.run(
        service.spawn_child(
            _orchestration_request(),
            parent_session_id="parent-session",
            body=body,
        )
    )
    second = asyncio.run(
        service.spawn_child(
            _orchestration_request(),
            parent_session_id="parent-session",
            body=body,
        )
    )

    assert second.delegation_id == first.delegation_id
    assert second.child_session_id == first.child_session_id
    assert second.status == first.status
    assert (
        db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM thread_delegations").fetchone()["n"] == 1
    )
    assert db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM sessions").fetchone()["n"] == 2
    assert db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM workspaces").fetchone()["n"] == 2


def test_duplicate_spawn_with_mismatched_request_conflicts(db, git_repo) -> None:
    """One key reuse with a different normalized request is rejected."""
    from yinshi.services.thread_orchestration import (
        ThreadIdempotencyConflictError,
        ThreadOrchestrationService,
    )

    seed_parent_stack(db, git_repo)
    service = ThreadOrchestrationService()

        service.spawn_child(

                idempotency_key=key,
                title="Same title",

                    idempotency_key=key,
                    title="Same title",
                    task="Different task",
                    start_immediately=False,
                ),
            )
        )

        db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM thread_delegations").fetchone()["n"] == 1
    )

Yinshi is a web app for managing coding agent workspaces. Users can import GitHub or local git repositories as "workspaces," spawn git worktrees with random branch names, and interact with a `pi` coding agent (https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/tree/main). All data (conversations, plans, pi configs, worktrees) is stored in SQLite.

## Tech Stack

- **Backend**: Python (FastAPI), SQLite
- **Frontend**: Next.js
- **Agent**: pi coding agent integration

## Architecture

- Python conventions and patterns are defined in `PYTHON.md` -- follow it for all backend code
- Follow the `src/` layout from `PYTHON.md` for the Python backend
- Use pydantic for data validation and settings management
- Use async/await for I/O-bound operations
- Use parameterized queries for all SQLite access

## Development

```bash
# Python backend
python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements/dev.txt
pytest --cov=src
black src tests && isort src tests && flake8 src tests && mypy src

# Run single test
pytest tests/path/to/test_file.py::test_name -v

# Frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

## Design Principles

- "Don't make me think" -- consistent, simple UX
- No frills, just performance
- No plan mode, commits, or file change history -- focus on agent interaction only

## Key Files

- `GOAL.md` -- full project requirements and vision
- `PYTHON.md` -- Python coding standards (error handling, type hints, async, testing, logging)

Phase 3 of the thread orchestration plan. This service owns the spawn
workflow: idempotent delegation reservation under ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE``,
child workspace provisioning through ``ThreadWorkspaceService``, and child
session creation. No SQLite transaction stays open while Git commands run.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
from dataclasses import dataclass

from fastapi import Request

from yinshi.api.deps import get_db_for_request, get_tenant, run_db_operation_for_request
from yinshi.exceptions import YinshiError
from yinshi.model_catalog import normalize_model_ref
from yinshi.models import ThreadChildCreate
from yinshi.services.thread_lifecycle import DELEGATION_STATUS_PROVISIONING, DELEGATION_STATUS_QUEUED
from yinshi.services.thread_queries import ThreadNotFoundError
from yinshi.services.thread_workspaces import ThreadWorkspaceService


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ThreadSpawnOutcome:
    """Stable spawn result for one idempotency key."""

    delegation_id: str
    status: str
    child_session_id: str | None


class ThreadOrchestrationError(YinshiError):
    """Base class for orchestration failures carrying one safe error code."""

    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str) -> None:
        assert code, "safe error code must not be empty"
        super().__init__(message)
        self.code = code


class ThreadIdempotencyConflictError(ThreadOrchestrationError):
    """Raised when one idempotency key is reused with a different request."""

    def __init__(self, message: str = "idempotency key was already used") -> None:
        super().__init__("idempotency_key_conflict", message)


class ThreadOrchestrationService:
    """Coordinate the manual child-thread lifecycle."""

    def __init__(self, workspaces: ThreadWorkspaceService | None = None) -> None:
        self._workspaces = workspaces or ThreadWorkspaceService()

    async def spawn_child(
        self,
        request: Request,
        *,
        parent_session_id: str,
        body: ThreadChildCreate,
    ) -> ThreadSpawnOutcome:
        """Reserve, provision, and attach one manual child thread."""
        if not isinstance(parent_session_id, str) or not parent_session_id.strip():
            raise ValueError("parent_session_id must be a non-empty string")
        reservation = await run_db_operation_for_request(
            request,
            lambda db: self._reserve(db, parent_session_id, body),
        )
        if str(reservation["status"]) != DELEGATION_STATUS_PROVISIONING:
            return ThreadSpawnOutcome(
                delegation_id=str(reservation["id"]),
                status=str(reservation["status"]),
                child_session_id=(
                    None
                    if reservation["child_session_id"] is None
                    else str(reservation["child_session_id"])
                ),
            )
        outcome = await self._provision_and_attach(request, reservation=reservation)
        return outcome

    def _reserve(
        self,
        db: sqlite3.Connection,
        parent_session_id: str,
        body: ThreadChildCreate,
    ) -> sqlite3.Row:
        """Insert one provisioning delegation inside one immediate transaction."""
        db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        try:
            parent = db.execute(
                "SELECT id, workspace_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?",
                (parent_session_id,),
            ).fetchone()
            if parent is None:
                raise ThreadNotFoundError(parent_session_id)
            existing = db.execute(
                """SELECT * FROM thread_delegations
                   WHERE parent_session_id = ? AND idempotency_key = ?""",
                (parent_session_id, body.idempotency_key),
            ).fetchone()
            if existing is not None:
                db.rollback()
                _assert_request_matches(existing, body)
                return existing
            db.execute(
                """INSERT INTO thread_delegations (
                       parent_session_id, idempotency_key, initiator,
                       title, task, context, role,
                       requested_model, requested_thinking, status
                   ) VALUES (?, ?, 'user', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                (
                    parent_session_id,
                    body.idempotency_key,
                    body.title.strip(),
                    body.task.strip(),
                    None if body.context is None else body.context.strip(),
                    body.role,
                    normalize_model_ref(body.model),
                    body.thinking,
                    DELEGATION_STATUS_PROVISIONING,
                ),
            )
            row = db.execute(
                """SELECT * FROM thread_delegations
                   WHERE parent_session_id = ? AND idempotency_key = ?""",
                (parent_session_id, body.idempotency_key),
            ).fetchone()
            db.commit()
            return row
        except BaseException:
            db.rollback()
            raise

    async def _provision_and_attach(
        self,
        request: Request,
        *,
        reservation: sqlite3.Row,
    ) -> ThreadSpawnOutcome:
        """Provision the child workspace, then attach the child session."""
        tenant = get_tenant(request)
        # Git must run with no open SQLite transaction.
        with get_db_for_request(request) as db:
            provisioned = await self._workspaces.provision_child(
                db,
                tenant,
                parent_workspace_id=str(reservation["parent_session_id"] and _parent_workspace_id(db, reservation)),
                delegation_id=str(reservation["id"]),
            )

        def attach(db: sqlite3.Connection) -> str:
            db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            try:
                cursor = db.execute(
                    """INSERT INTO sessions (workspace_id, status, model,
                                             pi_context_version, title)
                       VALUES (?, 'idle', ?, 1, ?)""",
                    (provisioned.workspace_id, reservation["requested_model"], reservation["title"]),
                )
                child_session_id = str(db.execute(
                    "SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE rowid = ?",
                    (cursor.lastrowid,),
                ).fetchone()["id"])
                db.execute(
                    """UPDATE thread_delegations
                       SET child_session_id = ?, child_workspace_id = ?,
                           base_kind = ?, base_commit = ?, snapshot_ref = ?,
                           status = ?
                       WHERE id = ? AND status = ?""",
                    (
                        child_session_id,
                        provisioned.workspace_id,
                        provisioned.base_kind,
                        provisioned.base_commit,
                        provisioned.snapshot_ref,
                        DELEGATION_STATUS_QUEUED,
                        reservation["id"],
                        DELEGATION_STATUS_PROVISIONING,
                    ),
                )
                db.commit()
                return child_session_id
            except BaseException:
                db.rollback()
                raise

        child_session_id = await run_db_operation_for_request(request, attach)
        return ThreadSpawnOutcome(
            delegation_id=str(reservation["id"]),
            status=DELEGATION_STATUS_QUEUED,
            child_session_id=child_session_id,
        )


def _assert_request_matches(row: sqlite3.Row, body: ThreadChildCreate) -> None:
    """Reject one idempotency key reuse whose normalized request differs."""
    stored = {
        "title": str(row["title"] or "").strip(),
        "task": str(row["task"] or "").strip(),
        "context": (None if row["context"] is None else str(row["context"]).strip() or None),
        "role": str(row["role"]),
        "model": normalize_model_ref(str(row["requested_model"] or "")),
        "thinking": (
            None if row["requested_thinking"] is None else str(row["requested_thinking"])
        ),
    }
    incoming = {
        "title": body.title.strip(),
        "task": body.task.strip(),
        "context": None if body.context is None else body.context.strip() or None,
        "role": body.role,
        "model": normalize_model_ref(body.model),
        "thinking": body.thinking,
    }
    if stored != incoming:
        raise ThreadIdempotencyConflictError(
            "idempotency key was already used with a different request",
        )


def _parent_workspace_id(db: sqlite3.Connection, reservation: sqlite3.Row) -> str:
    """Resolve the parent session's workspace id."""
    row = db.execute(
        "SELECT workspace_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?",
        (str(reservation["parent_session_id"]),),
    ).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        raise ThreadNotFoundError(str(reservation["parent_session_id"]))
    return str(row["workspace_id"])

Pure domain policy for the thread orchestration layer. This module holds the
delegation status vocabulary and the legal transitions between statuses. It
deliberately performs no I/O so every caller shares one definition of the
Phase 3 state machine from the thread orchestration plan.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid

DELEGATION_STATUS_PROVISIONING = "provisioning"
DELEGATION_STATUS_QUEUED = "queued"
DELEGATION_STATUS_RUNNING = "running"
DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLING = "cancelling"
DELEGATION_STATUS_COMPLETED = "completed"
DELEGATION_STATUS_FAILED = "failed"
DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLED = "cancelled"
DELEGATION_STATUS_INTERRUPTED = "interrupted"

TERMINAL_DELEGATION_STATUSES = frozenset(
    {
        DELEGATION_STATUS_COMPLETED,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_FAILED,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLED,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_INTERRUPTED,
    }
)


def is_terminal_delegation_status(status: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether one delegation status can never change again."""
    return status in TERMINAL_DELEGATION_STATUSES


# A cancellation that loses to completion preserves the completion.
_ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {
    DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLING: frozenset({DELEGATION_STATUS_COMPLETED}),
}


def can_transition(current: str, target: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether one delegation status may move to another."""
    return target in _ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.get(current, frozenset())


def cancellation_target(status: str) -> str:
    """Return the stable resulting status when cancellation is requested."""
    targets = {
        DELEGATION_STATUS_PROVISIONING: DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLED,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_QUEUED: DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLED,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_RUNNING: DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLING,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLING: DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLING,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_COMPLETED: DELEGATION_STATUS_COMPLETED,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_FAILED: DELEGATION_STATUS_FAILED,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLED: DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLED,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_INTERRUPTED: DELEGATION_STATUS_INTERRUPTED,
    }
    return targets[status]


def initial_run_idempotency_key(delegation_id: str) -> str:
    """Derive the deterministic initial prompt-run idempotency key."""
    normalized = str(delegation_id).strip().lower()
    if (
        len(normalized) != 32
        or any(character not in "0123456789abcdef" for character in normalized)
    ):
        raise ValueError("delegation_id must be 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters")
    return str(
        uuid.uuid5(uuid.NAMESPACE_URL, f"yinshi:thread-initial-run:{normalized}")
    )

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import uuid

import pytest
from fastapi import Request

from tests.test_thread_workspaces import head_commit, seed_parent_stack
from yinshi.models import ThreadChildCreate

from yinshi.services.thread_lifecycle import (
    cancellation_target,
    can_transition,
    initial_run_idempotency_key,
    is_terminal_delegation_status,
)


def test_terminal_delegation_status_set_is_exact() -> None:
    """Only completed, failed, cancelled, and interrupted are terminal."""
    assert is_terminal_delegation_status("completed")
    assert is_terminal_delegation_status("failed")
    assert is_terminal_delegation_status("cancelled")
    assert is_terminal_delegation_status("interrupted")
    assert not is_terminal_delegation_status("provisioning")
    assert not is_terminal_delegation_status("queued")
    assert not is_terminal_delegation_status("running")
    assert not is_terminal_delegation_status("cancelling")


def test_cancellation_losing_to_completion_preserves_completion() -> None:
    """A cancelling delegation may still resolve to completed."""
    assert can_transition("cancelling", "completed")


def test_cancellation_targets_are_stable_per_status() -> None:
    """Cancellation resolves each status to its plan-stable target."""
    assert cancellation_target("provisioning") == "cancelled"
    assert cancellation_target("queued") == "cancelled"
    assert cancellation_target("running") == "cancelling"
    assert cancellation_target("cancelling") == "cancelling"
    assert cancellation_target("completed") == "completed"
    assert cancellation_target("failed") == "failed"
    assert cancellation_target("cancelled") == "cancelled"
    assert cancellation_target("interrupted") == "interrupted"


def test_initial_run_idempotency_key_is_deterministic_canonical_uuid() -> None:
    """The initial child run derives one stable canonical UUID from the delegation."""
    delegation_id = "d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f801"
    first = initial_run_idempotency_key(delegation_id)
    assert first == initial_run_idempotency_key(delegation_id)
    assert str(uuid.UUID(first)) == first
    assert first != initial_run_idempotency_key("d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f802")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        initial_run_idempotency_key("not-a-delegation-id")

def test_spawn_child_reserves_and_provisions_a_queued_child(db, git_repo) -> None:
    """One spawn reserves, provisions, and attaches a queued child thread."""
    from yinshi.services.thread_orchestration import ThreadOrchestrationService

    seed_parent_stack(db, git_repo)
    service = ThreadOrchestrationService()
    body = ThreadChildCreate(
        idempotency_key=str(uuid.uuid4()),
        title="Implement OAuth validation",
        task="Implement state validation.",
        role="implementation",
        model="model-x",
        start_immediately=False,
    )

    outcome = asyncio.run(
        service.spawn_child(
            _orchestration_request(),
            parent_session_id="parent-session",
            body=body,
        )
    )

    delegation = db.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM thread_delegations WHERE id = ?", (outcome.delegation_id,)
    ).fetchone()

    assert delegation["status"] == "queued"
    assert delegation["initiator"] == "user"
    assert delegation["base_kind"] == "head"
    assert delegation["base_commit"] == head_commit(git_repo)
    child = db.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM sessions WHERE id = ?", (delegation["child_session_id"],)
    ).fetchone()
    assert child is not None
    assert child["title"] == "Implement OAuth validation"
    assert child["model"] == "model-x"
    workspace = db.execute(

    assert workspace is not None
    assert workspace["kind"] == "delegated"
    assert workspace["parent_workspace_id"] == "parent-ws"
    assert workspace["branch"] == f"yinshi/thread-{outcome.delegation_id[:8]}"

def test_duplicate_spawn_with_same_key_returns_the_same_child(db, git_repo) -> None:
    """One idempotency key resolves to exactly one delegation and child."""
    from yinshi.services.thread_orchestration import ThreadOrchestrationService

    seed_parent_stack(db, git_repo)
    service = ThreadOrchestrationService()
    body = ThreadChildCreate(
        idempotency_key=str(uuid.uuid4()),
        title="Implement OAuth validation",
        task="Implement state validation.",
        start_immediately=False,
    )

    first = asyncio.run(
        service.spawn_child(
            _orchestration_request(),
            parent_session_id="parent-session",
            body=body,
        )
    )
    second = asyncio.run(
        service.spawn_child(
            _orchestration_request(),
            parent_session_id="parent-session",
            body=body,
        )
    )

    assert second.delegation_id == first.delegation_id
    assert second.child_session_id == first.child_session_id
    assert second.status == first.status
    assert (
        db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM thread_delegations").fetchone()["n"] == 1
    )

def test_duplicate_spawn_with_mismatched_request_conflicts(db, git_repo) -> None:
    """One key reuse with a different normalized request is rejected."""
    from yinshi.services.thread_orchestration import (
        ThreadIdempotencyConflictError,
        ThreadOrchestrationService,

    seed_parent_stack(db, git_repo)
    service = ThreadOrchestrationService()

        service.spawn_child(

Status: Frozen through Phase 2.

Source: `yinshi-thread-orchestration-plan.md`, based on commit `e18c86948f533ffb002bd6ca46118b8ee3fcaafb`.

This release adds database records, read APIs, and isolated child workspace services. It does not run delegated agents.

## Terms and ownership

A thread is an existing Yinshi session used as one reasoning or work unit. A root thread has no parent delegation. A child thread is referenced by `thread_delegations.child_session_id`.

A delegation records the durable parent-to-child task relationship. A result stores a bounded report with Git metadata. A workspace remains the filesystem and Git execution environment.

Each thread has exactly one session. Each child has at most one parent. Existing sessions without delegation records remain valid roots.

Parentage comes only from `thread_delegations.child_session_id`. The `sessions` table does not store a parent ID. Public APIs never reparent existing sessions.

Parent and child must share one tenant, repository, and runtime location. Backend code enforces depth and count limits. Bounded reads reject cycles and excessive trees.

A workspace cannot be deleted while one of its sessions owns a child delegation. The API returns HTTP 409 with `thread_children_present`.

## Limits and flags

| Setting | Default |
| --- | ---: |
| `THREAD_MAX_DEPTH` | 1 |
| `THREAD_MAX_DIRECT_CHILDREN` | 4 |
| `THREAD_MAX_ACTIVE_DESCENDANTS` | 4 |
| `THREAD_MAX_TOTAL` | 20 |
| `THREAD_MAX_SPAWNS_PER_TURN` | 4 |
| `THREAD_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS_MAX` | 60 |
| `THREAD_SNAPSHOT_MAX_FILES` | 20,000 |
| `THREAD_SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES` | 1 GiB |

`THREAD_HIERARCHY_ENABLED` defaults to `true`. Disabled hierarchy routes return 404. `AGENT_DELEGATION_ENABLED` defaults to `false`.

All numeric limits must be positive. Maximum depth cannot exceed 32. Total capacity must exceed direct-child and active-descendant capacity because it includes the root.

## State rules

Delegations start in `provisioning`. They may advance through `queued` and `running` before reaching a terminal state.

Valid terminal states are `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, and `interrupted`. Cancellation can use `cancelling` between `running` and `cancelled`.

Active counts include `provisioning`, `queued`, `running`, and `cancelling`. A provisioning record without a child session reserves capacity and appears as a placeholder.

Later recursive deletion must remove deepest descendants first. Parent workspaces are removed last. Phase 1 rejects parent deletion instead.

## Database contract

Shared databases use schema version 6. Per-user databases use user version 2. Both migration paths support SQLite and SQLCipher.

Migrations are additive and repeatable. Existing rows remain unchanged. Older restored databases migrate when opened. Whole-file backup and relay transfer require no format conversion.

Existing tables gain these fields:

```sql
ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN title TEXT;
ALTER TABLE workspaces ADD COLUMN kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user';
ALTER TABLE workspaces ADD COLUMN parent_workspace_id TEXT;
```

Workspace kinds are `user`, `delegated`, and `integration`. Existing rows use `user`.

`thread_delegations` stores parent and child session IDs, child workspace ID, request data, model choices, status, Git base data, timestamps, retry lineage, and safe errors.

The child session ID is unique. Parent deletion uses `ON DELETE RESTRICT`. Child deletion cascades to its delegation. Parent and idempotency key form a unique pair.

`thread_results` uses the delegation ID as its primary key. It stores versioned JSON lists, summary text, Git refs, seal state, and timestamps.

Result deletion follows delegation deletion. Public result reads return sealed rows only.

## Read API

Thread routes use the same authenticated database and ownership checks as session routes.

| Method | Route | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/threads/{session_id}` | One thread projection |
| `GET` | `/api/threads/{session_id}/tree` | Root, descendants, placeholders, and counts |
| `GET` | `/api/threads/{session_id}/children` | Direct child projections |
| `GET` | `/api/threads/{session_id}/result` | Sealed child result |
| `GET` | `/api/threads/{session_id}/limits` | Configured limits and current usage |

A thread projection contains IDs, depth, title, role, origin, state, workspace ID, model, child counts, spawn allowance, and creation time.

Roots use session status and `user` origin. Delegated children use delegation status and initiator origin.

A tree request accepts any member ID. The response always identifies the actual root and returns the complete bounded tree. Nodes preserve their actual parent ID.

Counts include placeholders because each placeholder reserves a possible child. Limit calculations use totals from the actual root, even when requested for a child.

A result request returns 404 when no sealed result exists. Existing session routes keep their prior behavior and gain optional title input and output.

Responses use Pydantic models. Tree expansion stops after 500 descendants or placeholders. Ancestry traversal stops after 32 parent links.

## Security and failure behavior

Tenant mode uses one database per user. Legacy mode applies repository ownership checks before returning thread data.

A malformed cross-owner relationship cannot disclose foreign session metadata. Unknown sessions and unauthorized records return 404.

Requests cannot supply tenant IDs, runtime locations, filesystem paths, branch names, Git refs, parent workspace IDs, credentials, or capabilities.

Errors do not include raw database, filesystem, or credential details. Cycles and oversized trees stop processing instead of returning partial data.

The deletion guard runs before cancellation, sidecar release, container removal, worktree deletion, or session-file deletion. A second service check protects direct callers. Foreign keys provide the final storage check.

## Isolated workspace service

`ThreadWorkspaceService` provides child provisioning, Git finalization, and idempotent cleanup. Phase 3 will call these operations after reserving a delegation.

Clean parents use their exact `HEAD`. Dirty parents use a synthetic commit built through a private alternate Git index.

Dirty snapshots include tracked changes and permitted untracked files. Ignored files remain excluded. Protected `.env` paths cause rejection.

Tracked symlinks remain Git symlink blobs. Snapshot creation never follows their targets. Dirty submodules cause rejection.

Snapshot commits use `refs/yinshi/snapshots/<delegation-id>`. Result commits use `refs/yinshi/results/<delegation-id>`.

Hidden refs use atomic create-only publication. A competing writer keeps ownership of its ref.

Child branches use `yinshi/thread-<short-delegation-id>`. Worktrees start from the exact base commit and receive `kind = delegated` with their parent workspace ID.

Provisioning holds the repository lifecycle lock. It preserves parent `HEAD`, branch, index, staged state, working files, and untracked files.

Cleanup removes only artifacts owned by its delegation. It preserves pre-existing branches, worktrees, and result refs after failed provisioning.

Finalization captures committed and uncommitted child state in one synthetic result commit. Its parent is the recorded base commit.

Result refs are immutable. A retry reuses a result only when its tree and parent match.

Changed-file output supports additions, modifications, deletions, copies, and renames. It stops above 5,000 entries.

Child-only cleanup and finalization reject ordinary user workspaces. Repository and workspace roots cannot use symlink indirection.

## Deferred work

Phase 3 adds manual spawn, child sessions, orchestration writes, and prompt execution. Phases 4 and 5 add sidecar protocol support and agent tools.

Later work adds cancellation, retry, reporting, recursive deletion, managed runtime integration, nested delegation, budgets, waiting, and automated result sealing.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

Yinshi is a web app for managing coding agent workspaces. Users can import GitHub or local git repositories as "workspaces," spawn git worktrees with random branch names, and interact with a `pi` coding agent (https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/tree/main). All data (conversations, plans, pi configs, worktrees) is stored in SQLite.

## Tech Stack

- **Backend**: Python (FastAPI), SQLite
- **Frontend**: Next.js
- **Agent**: pi coding agent integration

## Architecture

- Python conventions and patterns are defined in `PYTHON.md` -- follow it for all backend code
- Follow the `src/` layout from `PYTHON.md` for the Python backend
- Use pydantic for data validation and settings management
- Use async/await for I/O-bound operations
- Use parameterized queries for all SQLite access

## Development

```bash
# Python backend
python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements/dev.txt
pytest --cov=src
black src tests && isort src tests && flake8 src tests && mypy src

# Run single test
pytest tests/path/to/test_file.py::test_name -v

# Frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

## Design Principles

- "Don't make me think" -- consistent, simple UX
- No frills, just performance
- No plan mode, commits, or file change history -- focus on agent interaction only

## Key Files

- `GOAL.md` -- full project requirements and vision
- `PYTHON.md` -- Python coding standards (error handling, type hints, async, testing, logging)

Phase 3 of the thread orchestration plan. This service owns the spawn
workflow: idempotent delegation reservation under ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE``,
child workspace provisioning through ``ThreadWorkspaceService``, and child
session creation. No SQLite transaction stays open while Git commands run.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
from dataclasses import dataclass

from fastapi import Request

from yinshi.api.deps import get_db_for_request, get_tenant, run_db_operation_for_request
from yinshi.exceptions import YinshiError
from yinshi.model_catalog import normalize_model_ref
from yinshi.models import ThreadChildCreate
from yinshi.services.thread_lifecycle import DELEGATION_STATUS_PROVISIONING, DELEGATION_STATUS_QUEUED
from yinshi.services.thread_queries import ThreadNotFoundError
from yinshi.services.thread_workspaces import ThreadWorkspaceService


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ThreadSpawnOutcome:
    """Stable spawn result for one idempotency key."""

    delegation_id: str
    status: str
    child_session_id: str | None


class ThreadOrchestrationError(YinshiError):
    """Base class for orchestration failures carrying one safe error code."""

    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str) -> None:
        assert code, "safe error code must not be empty"
        super().__init__(message)
        self.code = code


class ThreadIdempotencyConflictError(ThreadOrchestrationError):
    """Raised when one idempotency key is reused with a different request."""

    def __init__(self, message: str = "idempotency key was already used") -> None:
        super().__init__("idempotency_key_conflict", message)


class ThreadOrchestrationService:
    """Coordinate the manual child-thread lifecycle."""

    def __init__(self, workspaces: ThreadWorkspaceService | None = None) -> None:
        self._workspaces = workspaces or ThreadWorkspaceService()

    async def spawn_child(
        self,
        request: Request,
        *,
        parent_session_id: str,
        body: ThreadChildCreate,
    ) -> ThreadSpawnOutcome:
        """Reserve, provision, and attach one manual child thread."""
        if not isinstance(parent_session_id, str) or not parent_session_id.strip():
            raise ValueError("parent_session_id must be a non-empty string")
        reservation = await run_db_operation_for_request(
            request,
            lambda db: self._reserve(db, parent_session_id, body),
        )
        if str(reservation["status"]) != DELEGATION_STATUS_PROVISIONING:
            return ThreadSpawnOutcome(
                delegation_id=str(reservation["id"]),
                status=str(reservation["status"]),
                child_session_id=(
                    None
                    if reservation["child_session_id"] is None
                    else str(reservation["child_session_id"])
                ),
            )
        outcome = await self._provision_and_attach(request, reservation=reservation)
        return outcome

    def _reserve(
        self,
        db: sqlite3.Connection,
        parent_session_id: str,
        body: ThreadChildCreate,
    ) -> sqlite3.Row:
        """Insert one provisioning delegation inside one immediate transaction."""
        db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        try:
            parent = db.execute(
                "SELECT id, workspace_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?",
                (parent_session_id,),
            ).fetchone()
            if parent is None:
                raise ThreadNotFoundError(parent_session_id)
            existing = db.execute(
                """SELECT * FROM thread_delegations
                   WHERE parent_session_id = ? AND idempotency_key = ?""",
                (parent_session_id, body.idempotency_key),
            ).fetchone()
            if existing is not None:
                db.rollback()
                _assert_request_matches(existing, body)
                return existing
            db.execute(
                """INSERT INTO thread_delegations (
                       parent_session_id, idempotency_key, initiator,
                       title, task, context, role,
                       requested_model, requested_thinking, status
                   ) VALUES (?, ?, 'user', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                (
                    parent_session_id,
                    body.idempotency_key,
                    body.title.strip(),
                    body.task.strip(),
                    None if body.context is None else body.context.strip(),
                    body.role,
                    normalize_model_ref(body.model),
                    body.thinking,
                    DELEGATION_STATUS_PROVISIONING,
                ),
            )
            row = db.execute(
                """SELECT * FROM thread_delegations
                   WHERE parent_session_id = ? AND idempotency_key = ?""",
                (parent_session_id, body.idempotency_key),
            ).fetchone()
            db.commit()
            return row
        except BaseException:
            db.rollback()
            raise

    async def _provision_and_attach(
        self,
        request: Request,
        *,
        reservation: sqlite3.Row,
    ) -> ThreadSpawnOutcome:
        """Provision the child workspace, then attach the child session."""
        tenant = get_tenant(request)
        # Git must run with no open SQLite transaction.
        with get_db_for_request(request) as db:
            provisioned = await self._workspaces.provision_child(
                db,
                tenant,
                parent_workspace_id=str(reservation["parent_session_id"] and _parent_workspace_id(db, reservation)),
                delegation_id=str(reservation["id"]),
            )

        def attach(db: sqlite3.Connection) -> str:
            db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            try:
                cursor = db.execute(
                    """INSERT INTO sessions (workspace_id, status, model,
                                             pi_context_version, title)
                       VALUES (?, 'idle', ?, 1, ?)""",
                    (provisioned.workspace_id, reservation["requested_model"], reservation["title"]),
                )
                child_session_id = str(db.execute(
                    "SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE rowid = ?",
                    (cursor.lastrowid,),
                ).fetchone()["id"])
                db.execute(
                    """UPDATE thread_delegations
                       SET child_session_id = ?, child_workspace_id = ?,
                           base_kind = ?, base_commit = ?, snapshot_ref = ?,
                           status = ?
                       WHERE id = ? AND status = ?""",
                    (
                        child_session_id,
                        provisioned.workspace_id,
                        provisioned.base_kind,
                        provisioned.base_commit,
                        provisioned.snapshot_ref,
                        DELEGATION_STATUS_QUEUED,
                        reservation["id"],
                        DELEGATION_STATUS_PROVISIONING,
                    ),
                )
                db.commit()
                return child_session_id
            except BaseException:
                db.rollback()
                raise

        child_session_id = await run_db_operation_for_request(request, attach)
        return ThreadSpawnOutcome(
            delegation_id=str(reservation["id"]),
            status=DELEGATION_STATUS_QUEUED,
            child_session_id=child_session_id,
        )


def _assert_request_matches(row: sqlite3.Row, body: ThreadChildCreate) -> None:
    """Reject one idempotency key reuse whose normalized request differs."""
    stored = {
        "title": str(row["title"] or "").strip(),
        "task": str(row["task"] or "").strip(),
        "context": (None if row["context"] is None else str(row["context"]).strip() or None),
        "role": str(row["role"]),

import uuid

DELEGATION_STATUS_PROVISIONING = "provisioning"
DELEGATION_STATUS_QUEUED = "queued"
DELEGATION_STATUS_RUNNING = "running"
DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLING = "cancelling"
DELEGATION_STATUS_COMPLETED = "completed"
DELEGATION_STATUS_FAILED = "failed"
DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLED = "cancelled"
DELEGATION_STATUS_INTERRUPTED = "interrupted"

TERMINAL_DELEGATION_STATUSES = frozenset(
    {
        DELEGATION_STATUS_COMPLETED,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_FAILED,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLED,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_INTERRUPTED,
    }
)


def is_terminal_delegation_status(status: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether one delegation status can never change again."""
    return status in TERMINAL_DELEGATION_STATUSES


# A cancellation that loses to completion preserves the completion.
_ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {
    DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLING: frozenset({DELEGATION_STATUS_COMPLETED}),

    return target in _ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.get(current, frozenset())

    """Return the stable resulting status when cancellation is requested."""
    targets = {
        DELEGATION_STATUS_PROVISIONING: DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLED,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_QUEUED: DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLED,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_RUNNING: DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLING,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLING: DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLING,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_COMPLETED: DELEGATION_STATUS_COMPLETED,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_FAILED: DELEGATION_STATUS_FAILED,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLED: DELEGATION_STATUS_CANCELLED,
        DELEGATION_STATUS_INTERRUPTED: DELEGATION_STATUS_INTERRUPTED,
    }
    return targets[status]

def test_terminal_delegation_status_set_is_exact() -> None:
    """Only completed, failed, cancelled, and interrupted are terminal."""
    assert is_terminal_delegation_status("completed")
    assert is_terminal_delegation_status("failed")
    assert is_terminal_delegation_status("cancelled")
    assert is_terminal_delegation_status("interrupted")
    assert not is_terminal_delegation_status("provisioning")
    assert not is_terminal_delegation_status("queued")
    assert not is_terminal_delegation_status("running")
    assert not is_terminal_delegation_status("cancelling")


def test_cancellation_losing_to_completion_preserves_completion() -> None:
    """A cancelling delegation may still resolve to completed."""
    assert can_transition("cancelling", "completed")


def test_cancellation_targets_are_stable_per_status() -> None:
    """Cancellation resolves each status to its plan-stable target."""
    assert cancellation_target("provisioning") == "cancelled"
    assert cancellation_target("queued") == "cancelled"
    assert cancellation_target("running") == "cancelling"
    assert cancellation_target("cancelling") == "cancelling"
    assert cancellation_target("completed") == "completed"
    assert cancellation_target("failed") == "failed"
    assert cancellation_target("cancelled") == "cancelled"
    assert cancellation_target("interrupted") == "interrupted"


def test_initial_run_idempotency_key_is_deterministic_canonical_uuid() -> None:

    """One spawn reserves, provisions, and attaches a queued child thread."""
    from yinshi.services.thread_orchestration import ThreadOrchestrationService

    seed_parent_stack(db, git_repo)
    service = ThreadOrchestrationService()
    body = ThreadChildCreate(
        idempotency_key=str(uuid.uuid4()),
        title="Implement OAuth validation",
        task="Implement state validation.",

        model="model-x",

        service.spawn_child(

            parent_session_id="parent-session",

        "SELECT * FROM thread_delegations WHERE id = ?", (outcome.delegation_id,)
    ).fetchone()
